- `content/docs/data-modeling/queries.mdx`  _(via count_distinct (literal, a string literal in NUMERIC_RESULT_FUNCTIONS))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx`  _(via count_distinct (literal, a string literal in NUMERIC_RESULT_FUNCTIONS))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via count_distinct (literal, a string literal in NUMERIC_RESULT_FUNCTIONS))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **17** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 949e99bed9352d49a82aa186fffef86468a9d533` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4d7eb0a70dec7ec31588c29156abcbd72c868a92` — the merge of head `211cfba4770d5afbf78a31265412e481a38ae73e` into base `949e99bed9352d49a82aa186fffef86468a9d533`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4d7eb0a70dec7ec31588c29156abcbd72c868a92 && git checkout 4d7eb0a70dec7ec31588c29156abcbd72c868a92
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 949e99bed9352d49a82aa186fffef86468a9d533 211cfba4770d5afbf78a31265412e481a38ae73e && git checkout -B drift-repro 949e99bed9352d49a82aa186fffef86468a9d533 && git merge --no-ff 211cfba4770d5afbf78a31265412e481a38ae73e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 949e99bed9352d49a82aa186fffef86468a9d533
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 949e99bed9352d49a82aa186fffef86468a9d533` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `211cfba4770d5afbf78a31265412e481a38ae73e`

Scope: 7 files, +973/−26, on merge base `949e99bed9`:
- `engine.ts`: the import block, plus ONE hunk inside `ObjectQL.aggregate` (the per-aggregation `filter` loop and the `having` entry). `lowerWhereFilterArray` is untouched;
- `having-filter.ts` (+311/−12);
- two test files and three changesets.

`packages/spec`, the drivers, REST, `metadata-protocol` and `service-analytics` are untouched. No governed surface is touched.

Measured in detached worktrees at head and base, through `ObjectQL.aggregate` and `POST /api/v1/data/:object/query`, on a real `InMemoryDriver` and a real `SqlDriver`:
- a populated object (6 rows, 3 groups) and an empty one;
- grouped and ungrouped;
- `having` on both the native door and the fallback door;
- with driver calls counted.

That is 1,720 cells per tree.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The principle (a refusal belongs to the query, never to the data): RIGHT.** 1,048 of 1,052 head refusal cells fire with 0 driver calls. The other 4 are driver-sql's pre-existing `INVALID_FIELD` on an undeclared aggregation field, identical at base. Every refusal this PR adds answers identically on the empty and the populated object, on both drivers, engine and REST. At base, 100 of 244 refusal cells were raised only after a driver call.
- **#20122's walker refusals: RIGHT.** These shapes, at base, refused after one `find` on a populated table and answered `200 []` on an empty one: `$median`, `$nand`, `$regex`, `$like` with a dangling escape, `$ilike`, a non-`$` key beside an operator, `$median` under `$not`, a reference in an `$in` / `$nin` / `$contains` / `$exists` operand, and `addDays` 1.5 / `'7'`. Some also counted 0 or every row on a populated table without refusing. At head each one is `INVALID_FILTER` / 400, with 0 calls.
- **#20122's type door: RIGHT.** At base, type-mismatched values counted 0 silently. A `Symbol` under `$ne` counted every row, and under `$gt` it threw an uncoded `TypeError`. At head each is `INVALID_FILTER` / 400, rooted at `aggregations[i].filter`. A bigint in `$in` now counts the rows it names, and copy-on-write was confirmed: the caller's object is untouched.
- **The shape gate: RIGHT.** At head, a string, number, `true`, `false`, `0`, `''`, `Map`, `Date`, `Set`, `[]`, a condition array and `['and', …]` are all `INVALID_FILTER` / 400 with 0 calls. `undefined`, `null`, a plain object and a null-prototype object are byte-identical to base. REST refuses every JSON shape (`VALIDATION_FAILED`) at both trees.
- **#20123: RIGHT.** An unknown `having` key is refused at any depth, named with its position (`having.$or[1].totl`, `having.$not.totl`), with the columns listed and 0 calls. That includes a source column, a dotted path, and a key after a held `$or` branch. An unknown operator is still reported first.
- **#20127: RIGHT.** `aggregatedRowColumnClasses` derives each column's class from the spec's value-class sets. A day bucket is a date and a coarser bucket is text. `count` / `sum` / `avg` are numeric, and `min` / `max` take the field's class. The checks run in `applyCrossFieldComparison`'s order, in `driver-sql`'s words with a declared adaptation. Every non-temporal, mixed-class or non-numeric-offset pair is refused, and the temporal controls are unchanged. What is left unjudged is declared: `min` / `max` of a `formula` field, undeclared fields on a door that does not refuse them, and hosts with no registry.
- **Controls:** 47 shapes / 720 cells byte-identical at base and head. Across the whole matrix: 808 cells narrowed, 0 widened, 4 answer-changed (the bigint `$in`) and 16 refusal-wording changes.
- **The pins discriminate.** The ablations failed exactly as the dev reported: 19, 11, 12 and 11, then the shape gate 3 + 6 = 9 of 211. With both files at their base blobs, 62 failed and 149 passed. Every edit was restored by blob.
- **Scope: RIGHT.** `merge-tree` against `origin/main` `437bb0d7a8` is clean.
- **CI at this head:** 41 runs, 36 `success`, 5 `skipped`, 0 failed and 0 pending. All seven required contexts are `success`.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/objectql` `minor`, `fix(objectql)!:`, BREAKING, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` in the body and all three changesets: CORRECT.
- 808 cells narrowed and 0 widened.
- The bigint `$in` change is a wrong-answer correction toward what `where` and `having` already answer. It is declared in the 20122 changeset.
- There is no new export or type member: `having-filter.ts` is not re-exported.
- ADR-0087 dispositions: 20122 is `already-registered`, and the three ids exist in the registry. 20123 and 20127 are `no-migration-prescription`.
- `check-changeset-no-major --event <PR body>`: "✓ This diff introduces no `major` bump." and "✓ LEVEL AXIS: … `no (narrowing)` …" (exit 0).
- `check-adr-0087-registration`: "✓ 3 declared-breaking changeset(s), each carrying an ADR-0087 disposition." (exit 0).
- `check-empty-changeset`: exit 0.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The array question was ruled A (5832826252), and it is implemented.
- **The three changesets are TRUE sentence by sentence,** and the PR body is TRUE where measured.
- **Docs, pre-existing and not this PR's:**
  - `query-syntax.mdx` :92 and :136 still call `aggregations[].filter` "EXPERIMENTAL — not enforced", which was already false before this PR;
  - `queries.mdx` :671 says the query route forwards only `where` / `groupBy` / `aggregations`, but REST forwards `having` too.

  Both are for the docs lane.
- **#20123 uses `INVALID_FILTER`, not the card's non-ruling `INVALID_FIELD`.** That is consistent with every other `having` refusal, and it is accepted.
- **The dev's five out-of-scope findings are REAL,** reproduced at head on both drivers. Four have a `reach:` measured at the public REST door (`200` with zero counts). The seat files them as one class-closure card.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-20122-aggregate-filter-doors`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Bvd69VPa6puiNzzPUroDBx`

**VERDICT: PASS**
